findings.text: Work changes hands 5 times: Sales to Client success (after step 1); Client success to Admin (after step 2); Admin to Senior bookkeeper (after step 3); Senior bookkeeper to Practice manager (after step 4); Practice manager to Bookkeeper (after step 5).
findings.evidence: Compared "Who does it" for 5 pairs of consecutive steps.

findings.text: With 5 handoffs, information may be lost or work may sit between teams. Could one person or team handle more consecutive steps?
This process uses 4 different tools or systems: Email, Email and shared spreadsheet, Spreadsheet and accounting software, Accounting software.
Moving between 4 tools may mean the same information is re-entered in more than one place. Worth checking which details get typed twice.
findings.evidence: Three or more different tools listed.

findings.text: Step 1 "Send welcome email and intake form" moves work or information to someone else. Each hand-over is a point where work can wait or details can get lost.
Step 1 "Send welcome email and intake form" relies on Email. Manual tools often mean re-typing, searching for information, or version mix-ups.
Step 2 "Collect documents and logins" relies on Email and shared spreadsheet. Manual tools often mean re-typing, searching for information, or version mix-ups.
Step 3 "Enter client details in the practice and accounting systems" involves entering or copying information. Manual data entry often means the same information is typed more than once.
Step 3 "Enter client details in the practice and accounting systems" relies on Spreadsheet and accounting software. Manual tools often mean re-typing, searching for information, or version mix-ups.
Step 4 "Review documents and set up chart of accounts" is a checking step. Checks can be necessary, but repeated or late checks are a common form of waste. Could errors be prevented earlier instead?
Step 5 "Manager approves setup" involves an approval. Approvals often create queues while work waits for someone to sign off.
Step 5 "Manager approves setup" relies on Email. Manual tools often mean re-typing, searching for information, or version mix-ups.

improvements.sourceText: Root cause of "New clients take 3 or more days to send their documents": There is no standard document checklist or secure upload portal for new clients.
improvements.title: Send a document checklist with a secure upload link, plus an automatic reminder on day 2
improvements.behavior: Sends the document checklist and secure upload link with every welcome email, and checks upload status on day 2.
improvements.measure: Client documents complete on first request

improvements.sourceText: Step 3 "Enter client details in the practice and accounting systems" is the most likely bottleneck: work queues there longer than anywhere else. Worth finding out why it waits.
improvements.title: Reduce the queue before Step 3 "Enter client details in the practice and accounting systems"

improvements.sourceText: Step 3 "Enter client details in the practice and accounting systems" involves entering or copying information. Manual data entry often means the same information is typed more than once.
improvements.title: Remove re-typing of information in Step 3 "Enter client details in the practice and accounting systems"

improvements.sourceText: Step 5 "Manager approves setup" involves an approval. Approvals often create queues while work waits for someone to sign off.
improvements.title: Speed up or simplify the approval in Step 5 "Manager approves setup"
improvements.behavior: Approves standard client setups within one business day using the setup checklist.
improvements.outcome: Setups no longer wait for sign-off.
improvements.measure: Days from signed proposal to first close

improvements.behavior: Creates every new client through one intake form, which fills the practice and accounting systems automatically.

whys.problem: New clients take 3 or more days to send their documents

whys.answer: Clients are not sure exactly which documents to send.
The intake email lists the documents in one long paragraph with no checklist.
whys.evidence: Compared the current welcome email template.

whys.answer: There is no standard document checklist or secure upload portal for new clients.
whys.evidence: Confirmed with the client success team.

whys.rootCause: There is no standard document checklist or secure upload portal for new clients.
whys.fix: Send a document checklist with a secure upload link, plus an automatic reminder on day 2
